title: Implicit-adjoint finite-volume topology optimization of two-dimensional conjugate heat transfer
summary: Designing compact, high-efficiency thermal architectures requires resolving the competing demands of solid conduction, fluid convection, and flow resistance within highly constrained physical envelopes. Density-based topology optimization provides a systematic framework for synthesizing these coupled layouts, yet the reproducibility and numerical stability of the resulting designs depend critically on the underlying discrete solvers and adjoint sensitivity mechanics.
